analysis.title: Market & Strategy update – Q4 2026
key_insights: Global growth remains resilient but divergences among major economies are set to widen if energy prices and yields stay elevated. 67% of G20 economies are seeing accelerating growth.

The US economy is the strongest, driven by the AI capex boom supporting manufacturing and, indirectly, consumption. Consumption is supported by capital gains and a falling savings rate. Base case is strong but fragile growth.

The EU economy is resilient for now, but leading indicators are weakening, gas inventories are very low, and French political uncertainty could rise around upcoming elections. Energy dependence raises the odds of weakness.

China's data is underwhelming, with retail sales growing 0.4% YoY and fixed asset investment growth at its lowest in decades excluding COVID. The October Plenum could bring incremental support measures.
Japan benefits from loose monetary and fiscal policy, strong exports and domestic demand. Monetary policy is tightening but remains behind the curve.
Central banks have raised rates in response to energy-driven inflation. Aggressive further hikes are priced in, but whether they materialize depends mostly on energy prices.

Expected Fed hikes over the next year moved from 1.5 to 3.8 in the last month. The report considers it very unlikely the Fed hikes as much as priced, and expects an eventual dovish shift. More hikes are likely in the short term.

Oil has been the main driver of yields and tightening expectations. Oil is likely to stay supported because Iran has an incentive to keep uncertainty elevated, inventories are low and China is buying again. A retracement would let yields fall across the curve.
Developed market bonds are positively correlated to equities and have lost their diversifier role. Short-term yields are likely to top in Q4. The report will not take duration risk above 3-4 years.
US TIPS are more attractive than nominal bonds because inflation expectations are anchored while real yields have risen.
The Treasury has increased long-term bond buybacks in response to higher US yields, and additional measures are expected in Q4.
Credit spreads remain extremely tight but have begun widening in the riskiest segments. EM local currency debt has delivered positive returns in 2026 and is expected to keep outperforming DM bonds.

The USD is torn between the hawkish Fed and US strength on one side and the Treasury's interventionist stance on the other. A downside resolution is expected but needs a dovish Fed shift. Sideways action is likely meanwhile.
The JPY has bottomed and should rise against DM currencies, especially EUR and CHF, given real yield differentials.

US equities are consolidating with oversold breadth (26% of companies above their 50-day moving average) and bearish short-term sentiment. Seasonality turns positive into October, which points to an upward resolution in coming weeks. Longer-term indicators flash warning signs, so more caution is warranted as the market rallies into Q4.

Tech has re-emerged as the market leader and is expected to drive the next leg up. Semiconductors are likely to resume their rally after 3 months of consolidation, and MAG7 should keep doing well. Cyclicals should stabilise.

Favor Japanese over European equities. European equities are vulnerable if energy and rates stay elevated, with cyclicals with domestic exposure most at risk. Industrials combined with energy exposure remain attractive.
The EM equity rally is driven by AI. Chinese equities are rolling over pending government action. Indian equities still require patience despite attractive valuations.

Gold's bull market is intact per the report, but rising tightening expectations and real yields keep it under pressure. Sideways action is likely near term, with the uptrend close to reasserting itself.
Owning oil and gas is the best hedge for equity exposure, since a continued rise in energy prices is the biggest risk to growth and inflation. Indices are significantly under-allocated to energy.
Rising LNG export capacity and data center demand growth make a strong case for US natural gas producers. The uranium bull case is strengthening as shown in long-term contract pricing.
Bitcoin has bottomed and dips should be bought.

risk_factors: A continued rise in energy prices is the key risk to growth and inflation.
Further rises in yields would require more hikes being priced in.

French elections and spread widening given poor fiscal position.
Credit spreads are extremely tight and widening in the riskiest segments.
Longer-term equity indicators flash warning signs as the market rallies into Q4.
Chinese growth is weak and awaiting government action.
vol_and_positioning: Short-term sentiment is quite bearish and flows into cash equivalents have risen, which suggests the pain trade is higher into the strong seasonal period.
US equity breadth is oversold, with 26% of companies above their 50-day moving average.
Investors have piled back into gold.
Indices are significantly under-allocated to energy.
geopolitical: Persisting tensions in the Middle East have pushed energy prices up again, with Iran having an incentive to keep uncertainty elevated.
Trump could make big announcements ahead of the midterms given rising odds of a Democratic sweep.
French political uncertainty could rise given upcoming elections, with spread widening a risk given France's poor fiscal position.
The October Plenum in China could bring incremental measures to revive the economy.

tension_points.bull_case: Bearish short-term sentiment, oversold breadth and positive seasonality point to an upward resolution, with tech leading.
tension_points.bear_case: Longer-term indicators flash warning signs as the market rallies into Q4, so more caution is warranted.

tension_points.bull_case: The Fed's optimistic projections lay the ground for an eventual dovish shift, and pricing of 3.8 hikes is very unlikely to be met.
tension_points.bear_case: More hikes are likely in the short term, and the Fed wants to regain its credibility, delaying the dovish shift.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharp acceleration in energy prices would be needed for even more hikes to be priced in.
